tagline: A page Claude talks to you through when the terminal fails you
use_when: You can't comfortably read terminal output, you'd rather have one durable page per session than chat scrollback, or you're answering from your phone. It also starts on its own the first time Claude has a question or a check for you.
try_it: Use /proofs:working-log to start a working log for this session and post your updates there instead of in chat.

features.label: Always Know Where You Are
features.sub: A fixed top bar names the project, session and repo
features.title: A fixed top bar names the project, session and repo
features.what: A dark bar stays pinned at the top with the project name, the session name and the repository. With logs from several projects open, you can tell the tabs apart at a glance.
features.html: Acme Shop · checkout-fixacme/shop

features.label: Session Name First
features.sub: The session name leads the tab title and the top bar
features.title: The session name leads the tab title and the top bar
features.what: When several sessions run on one project, their logs would otherwise look identical. The session name goes first in the browser tab, where titles get cut off last, and is highlighted in the top bar, so you reply to the right one.
features.html:
checkout-fix· Acme Shop log
billing-bug· Acme Shop log
Same project, two sessions, no mix-ups

features.label: Did My Reload Land?
features.sub: A version marker shows you have the newest page
features.title: A version marker shows you have the newest page
features.what: The status bar reads like "v3 · updated Nov 2 · entry 14" and goes up with every republish. After you reload the same link, you can see at once whether the new version arrived.

features.label: Newest on Top
features.sub: The latest message is always the first thing you see
features.title: The latest message is always the first thing you see
features.what: Messages are listed newest first, each with a number, a title and a status chip such as Your move, Background, Queued or Done. You open the page and the thing that needs you is right there.

features.label: Headline, Then Detail
features.sub: One plain sentence first, the specifics underneath
features.title: One plain sentence first, the specifics underneath
features.what: Each message opens with a full-strength summary sentence, with the detail below in quieter text. You can skim the headlines and read deeper only where you need to.
features.html: The cart bug is fixed and tested.

features.label: Facts at a Glance
features.sub: A short bar of live facts: branch, tests, what's live, what's waiting
features.title: A short bar of live facts: branch, tests, what's live, what's waiting
features.what: Three or four current facts sit near the top: the working branch, whether tests pass, what is live, and what is waiting on you. You get the state of play without reading every message.

features.label: How to Get Back Here
features.sub: The exact command to reopen the page
features.title: The exact command to reopen the page
features.what: The page tells you how to reopen it, because you will close the tab: the exact command if your project has an opener script, or the place the project keeps its links. You don't have to dig for the link later.
features.html:

features.sub: A wide page, large text and big buttons and tick boxes
features.title: A wide page, large text and big buttons and tick boxes
features.what: The log uses most of a laptop screen with large body text, and the parts you actually click, the option buttons, note fields and tick boxes, are larger still. It is meant to be read comfortably, not squinted at.

features.title: A Read this tick per message dims what you've seen
features.what: Every message has a Read this tick that dims the card and updates the read count. What you haven't seen yet stands out from what you have.

features.what: Each message has its own note field, and there is one more box at the end for anything else. Your reply isn't limited to the options offered.

features.label: Close the Tab, Keep Your Place
features.sub: Ticks and answers are saved in your browser
features.title: Ticks and answers are saved in your browser
features.what: Your ticks, answers and notes survive a closed tab. They are saved per project and per session, so two logs open at once never overwrite each other.

features.label: What Failure Looks Like
features.sub: Any command you're asked to run comes with its error text
features.title: Any command you're asked to run comes with its error text
features.what: When a message asks you to run something, it shows what success prints and the most likely failure message. You can tell how it went even if your terminal is hard to read.

features.sub: Copy my replies puts everything on your clipboard
features.title: Copy my replies puts everything on your clipboard
features.what: One button copies plain text with every message marked read or unread, plus your answers and notes. You paste it into chat, which works even when reading the terminal doesn't.

features.label: The Paste Knows Where It's From
features.sub: Copied replies open with project, session, repo and time
features.title: Copied replies open with project, session, repo and time
features.what: The copied text starts with a short block naming the project, session, repository, the round of work and when you exported it. The session that receives it can tell straight away whether the reply belongs to it, and an old paste doesn't pass for a fresh one.

features.label: Same Link, Every Update
features.sub: Each update goes to the link you already have open
features.title: Each update goes to the link you already have open
features.what: The page is republished to the same link every time, from the same folder, so the tab you keep open just updates. A new link would leave you reading a stale page.
features.html: v1→v2→v3same link

features.label: Decided, Folded Away
features.sub: Answered questions leave the top at once
features.title: Answered questions leave the top at once
features.what: As soon as you answer a question, it leaves Waiting on you and becomes one line in Decided, folded at the bottom. Finished log entries go there too, or go entirely. The top of the page is always what still needs you.

features.label: Back on Track After a Reset
features.sub: After a reset, Claude updates your page instead of starting another
features.title: After a reset, Claude updates your page instead of starting another
features.what: If the conversation is reset mid-task, Claude looks up the log's saved link and updates that page rather than starting a second one you aren't looking at. Each session keeps its own log, so two sessions never overwrite each other's messages.
features.html:
Session resetlook up saved link
Same page updatedyour tab stays current

features.label: Tested Before You See It
features.sub: Every button is clicked and the layout looked at before publishing
features.title: Every button is clicked and the layout looked at before publishing
features.what: Before each publish the page is loaded and clicked through to confirm ticks, answers and the copied text all work, including the session name. Then one real screenshot at laptop and phone width checks that nothing scrolls sideways or squeezes text into a narrow column.
features.html: buttons work export has session no sideways scroll

features.label: Where the Page Goes
features.sub: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.title: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.what: Your project picks where review pages go: a private claude.ai link, an HTML file that opens in your browser, or that file served on your home Wi-Fi so a phone can open it. Nothing is ever uploaded or tunneled in the Wi-Fi mode, and the server stops when the review ends.
